## Appearance

Anne is a tall, slender woman with milk-white skin, a pointed face with a pretty nose, and shining, beautiful gray-green eyes. She has distinct, glossy hair—often called auburn or red—which she previously wore in long braids or short silky curls. Though she was self-conscious about her freckles and red hair in her youth, her expressive features and starry eyes give her a unique, dreamy charm.

## Personality

Anne is deeply imaginative, passionate, and romantic, often prone to daydreaming and intense emotions. In her youth, she was known for being heedless, energetic, and possessing a sharp temper when provoked. She is remarkably earnest, loyal, and understanding, holding high ideals and a strong desire to add beauty to the world around her. She has a tender heart and deep sympathy for others, particularly children and orphans, stemming from her own early life.

## History

Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne was orphaned early in life and endured an unhappy childhood as an unloved drudge before being taken in at Green Gables by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert. In Avonlea, she attended school, formed an intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, and established deep friendships, notably with Diana Barry. She attended Queen's Academy, where she earned her First Class License and won the Avery scholarship, before returning home to teach in Avonlea and found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Anne later attended Redmond College alongside friends like Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, earning her degree and winning the Thorburn Scholarship. After teaching in Summerside for three years, she married Gilbert Blythe in Green Gables and moved with him to their new home in Four Winds, later raising their children at Ingleside.

## Background by volume

- born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, to high school teacher Walter Shirley and Bertha Shirley  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>
- orphaned in infancy and spent a unhappy childhood as a drudge living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and in an asylum  <sub>[v1 c3 P43](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0043), [v1 c8 P43](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0043), [v4 c17 P5](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0005), [v5 c8 P5](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0005), [v5 c12 P12](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0012)</sub>
- adopted at age eleven by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Green Gables  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011), [v1 c6 P9](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0009), [v4 c2 P1](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0001)</sub>
- founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society  <sub>[v2 c6 P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v4 c1 P11](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0011)</sub>
- taught school in Summerside for three years  <sub>[v4 c1 P4](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0004)</sub>

## Quotes

> I was eleven last March. And I was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia. My father’s name was Walter Shirley, and he was a teacher in the Bolingbroke High School. My mother’s name was Bertha Shirley.  <sub>[v1 c5 P11](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0011)</sub>

> You see before you a perfectly happy person, Marilla. I’m perfectly happy—yes, in spite of my red hair. Just at present I have a soul above red hair.  <sub>[v1 c18 P48](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0048)</sub>

> To think that this is my twentieth birthday, and that I’ve left my teens behind me forever  <sub>[v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>
